newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Higher strikes busy on indices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Higher strikes busy on indices.

text.p: The focus of call activity in S&P 100 stock index .OEX moved to the 645 and 650 strikes on Thursday, from the 640s on Wednesday.
Traders said the market's rally -- the OEX ended up 3.73 points at 647.72 after climbing as high as 650.29 -- was the main reason for the focus on the higher strikes.
Similarly on the S&P 500 stock index .SPX, call activity picked up in the 675 and 680 strikes from the 665 and 670s.
The SPX gained 3.85 points to 671.13. It had reached a session high of 673.07.
On the OEX, the September 650 call was most active, with 22,665 contracts trading. Open interest through Wednesday was 25,864.
The September 645 call traded about 20,200 contracts, making it second most active. In addition, trading was heavy in the September 655, 660 and 640 calls.
In the October series, activity dropped off sharply, with the most active being the October 640 put, which traded just over 6,000 contracts.
In September, the busiest put was the 640, which traded roughly 15,800 contracts. With the market rallying, the option lost 1-3/8 to 2-5/8.
Despite the slowdown in October action, traders said investors continued to roll positions out in anticipation of the September 20 expiration of the September series.
But with the markets rallying, some were looking to book a quick profit on some of the September options before they expire, traders said.
